newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan opposition takes key town, bombs Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition takes key town, bombs Kabul.

text.p: The Afghan opposition alliance said on Sunday its forces had a taken a key town and a nearby airbase in a major rout of the Taleban militia north of the capital Kabul, which was also hit by a deadly air raid.

A Taleban spokesman, quoted by a Pakistan-based Afghan news service, confirmed the loss of the Charikar town 64 km (40 miles) from Kabul on Saturday night but had no word on the opposition report that its forces had also taken Bagram airbase on Sunday morning.
While fighting raged north of Kabul, a lone opposition jet bombed a suburb of the capital at midday on Sunday, killing at least seven people and wounding 12, residents at the scene said.
"Most dead and wounded came from a house where the owner was hosting a lunch for his friends and relatives," one said.
An opposition spokesman said earlier: "We captured Charikar at 9 p.m. (1630 GMT) on Saturday night and Bagram airbase at 9 this morning (0430 GMT)."
An official of the government ousted by Talebanm from Kabul last September told Reuters: "We closed the road and the Taleban could not withdraw any of their vehicles or equipment."
He said 500 Taleban fighters had been killed in the battle.
The official, who did not want to be named, was speaking by satellite telephone from the Panjsher valley stronghold of the ex-government's senior military commander Ahmed Shah Masood.
Journalists who tried to reach the area on Sunday morning were turned back by Taleban fighters.

The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted an un-named Taleban spokesman as saying the militia had lost control of Charikar, capital of Parawan province, but had sent 200 fresh soldiers to the front line near Bagram airbase and were pushing back opposition fighters.
Charikar fell to the Taleban in January, but has been under pressure from opposition forces for more than a month since they took the town of Jabal os-Siraj 70 km (45 miles) north of Kabul.
Charikar controls access to the Ghorband valley, where the Taleban are fighting forces of the Hezb-e-Wahdat faction, a mainly Shi'ite Moslem party in the opposition alliance.
Bagram airbase has long been Kabul's main military airfield, but it has been out of action for 10 months because it was too close to the front line.
The Taleban have been under continuous pressure since they briefly captured most of the opposition-held north of the country in May.
They have been gradually losing ground ever since. But they still control most of Afghanistan, including the capital, and are the most formidable single force in the country.

In the air raid, bombs hit the roof of a two-storey concrete house in Kabul's Khairkhana district, where relatives and neighbours were later digging through the rubble in search for survivors, witnesses said.
